lead: The most vibrant district in Valencia. From the 9th-century Arab garden to the epicentre of signature cuisine, contemporary art and the city’s most creative nightlife.

Ruzafa is today a multicultural, creative district where long-time residents live alongside a new generation of artists, designers and chefs. The bars that have been there forever compete with restaurants run by Michelin-starred cooks. Contemporary art galleries mingle with comic shops and bookshop-cafés. And its Mercat de Russafa, with more than a hundred stalls of fresh produce, remains the heart that beats at the centre of it all.
It is a district to get lost in. It has no visiting hours — it works at any time, from the esmorzaret at 10:00 to the last drink in the small hours.

items.title: Mercat de Russafa
items.subtitle: Julio Bellot and Javier Goerlich · 1954 · 100+ stalls · Colourful façade
items.body: The Mercat de Russafa is the backbone of the district. Opened in 1954 and designed by the architects Julio Bellot and Javier Goerlich, its colourful façade rises right opposite the Baroque church of San Valero and San Vicente Mártir, creating one of the most photogenic ensembles in Valencia. The market houses more than a hundred stalls with fresh local produce: fruit, vegetables, fish, meat, cured meats and flowers. On Mondays and Thursdays an open-air flea market is set up around it with vintage clothes, second-hand goods and seasonal plants. Its terraces are the perfect setting for the Valencian esmorzaret.

items.kicker: Food · From Ricard Camarena to world cuisine
items.title: Signature Cuisine and Esmorzaret
items.subtitle: Canalla Bistró · Mercat Bar · El Rus · International and traditional cuisine
items.body: Ruzafa is the most vibrant food district in Valencia. The leading Valencian chefs have set up their boldest ideas here. Ricard Camarena’s Canalla Bistró (Mestre Josep Serrano, 5) offers a culinary journey around the world with pastrami, causa limeña and eel nigiri in a relaxed setting. Quique Dacosta’s Mercat Bar (Joaquín Costa, 27) offers Valencian tapas in a setting inspired by market squares. For the esmorzaret, El Rus is the temple of the mid-morning breakfast, with the district’s most highly rated sandwich. The scene also includes Japanese, Mexican and Asian cuisine and Italian craft beer.

items.title: Street Art and Galleries
items.subtitle: Sporting Club Russafa · Espai Tactel · Sala Russafa · Color Elefante
items.body: The artistic revolution of Ruzafa is visible on every corner. The Sporting Club Russafa (Sevilla, 5) — a former boxing club — is now a non-profit creativity centre with exhibitions of contemporary art, dance, photography and workshops by local artists and craftspeople. The Sala Russafa is the district’s leading independent theatre: theatre, dance, classic cinema and crime-fiction conferences. The galleries Espai Tactel, Color Elefante, Trentatres Gallery, Maika Sánchez (Moratín, 15) and Imprevisual (Doctor Sumsi, 35) make up a first-rate contemporary art scene. Street art permeates the streets, especially around the market.

items.title: Parque Central
items.subtitle: Kathryn Gustafson · Inspired by Ausiàs March · Burying of the railway tracks
items.body: The Parque Central is Ruzafa’s most ambitious urban project and one of the most important in Valencia in decades. The first phase opened in 2018 on the space freed by burying the railway tracks. The design, chosen unanimously from 36 proposals from eight countries, is by the American landscape architect Kathryn Gustafson. The concept is inspired by Ausiàs March’s poem “Aigüa plena de seny”, with water, light and greenery taking centre stage. The park has large green areas, play spaces — including a vertical climbing wall — and opens from 8:00 to 21:00. When complete, it will cover more than 140,000 m².

items.kicker: Alternative shopping · Local design and vintage
items.title: Shopping, Bookshops and Design Stores
items.subtitle: Gnomo · Bartleby Libros · Utopik chocolates · Local designers’ shops
items.body: Ruzafa’s retail fabric is as distinctive as its food. Gnomo is the small family shop that brings together design objects, from shelves to rings and plants to give as gifts. The Bartleby bookshop (Cádiz, 50) combines selling books with an active cultural commitment. Utopik (Matías Perelló, 14) is the shop of Paco Llopis and Juana Rojas, two enthusiasts of artisan chocolate who work cocoa without additives — they even have chocolates shaped like Valencian firecrackers. The shops of young designers such as Siemprevivas and comic stores such as Gotham complete the alternative offering.

items.title: Fallas in Ruzafa · The streets Cuba and Literato Azorín
items.subtitle: First prizes for lighting · Light choreographies · Unique Fallas atmosphere
items.body: During the Fallas of Valencia, Ruzafa becomes one of the most spectacular epicentres of the festival. The district is especially known for the artistic quality of its lighting: the streets Cuba and Literato Azorín have won the first prizes for lighting in many consecutive years, with synchronised light choreographies that gather thousands of people. The district’s falla associations proudly maintain the identity of “la terra del ganxo” — Ruzafa’s historic nickname, from the workers who gathered wood from the Turia with hooks. The district’s fallas are among the most highly regarded for the quality of their monuments.

blocks.title: Tips for visiting Ruzafa
items: The esmorzaret at El Rus or on the terraces of the Mercat de Russafa is the best way to start the day in the district
The vintage flea market on Mondays and Thursdays is a classic: arrive before 10:00 for the best finds
Canalla Bistró and Mercat Bar fill up: book ahead if you want to eat there without waiting
The Fallas are the best time to visit Ruzafa: Cuba and Literato Azorín offer first-prize lighting
The Parque Central is perfect for a break between streets: it is open until 21:00 and has a climbing wall
Ruzafa works best without a map or a fixed plan: let yourself be led through the streets and go into whatever catches your eye
